newsitem.title: USA: United says occupancy encouraging for H2.
newsitem.headline: United says occupancy encouraging for H2.

text.p: United Dominion Realty Trust Inc said Friday higher occupancy levels in its 60,000 apartment homes are "encouraging" for the second half of the year.
The trust Friday reported its funds from operations rose to $29.0 million, or $0.33 a share, in the second quarter, compared with $17.0 million, or $0.30 a share, the year before.
Chief executive John McCann said the trust's operating results continued to improve in most of its markets because of solid rent growth.

"While occupancy levels in the quarter are below last year, we have experienced occupancy improvement throughout the first half of the year," McCann said in a statement. "In 16 of our 22 major markets, including our four largest, physical occupancy is higher in the second quarter than in the first. This is encouraging for the second half of the year."
United Dominion's second-quarter occupancy rates dropped, however, compared to the same quarter last year.

The trust's physical occupancy rates of 33,200 mature apartments in its Eastern division dropped to 93.3 percent in the second quarter from 94.0 percent in 1996. Occupancy rates of the 11,800 mature apartments of its Western division showed a decrease to 93.3 percent from 94.4 percent over the same period.
The trust's stock closed at 15-1/8 Thursday.
